subject: Throughput checklist & GPU recommendation path for VectorMed
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@vectormed.com>, Elena Torres <elena@vectormed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T14:05:00Z
Subject: Post-demo checklist: throughput targets, streaming & GPU path (VectorMed)

Samir / Elena — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed checklist so we can validate VectorMed's latency/throughput SLOs on dedicated capacity. Please confirm assumptions and priorities so we can lock the infra plan for the POC.

TL;DR: we recommend an initial validation across two GPU classes (A100 / H100-family) with a small verification run on L4 if cost sensitivity is high. Key knobs to validate: request concurrency, streaming chunk latency, and end-to-end 95th pct token latency for 512-token responses.

Assumptions from call:
- Typical prompt length: 180 tokens; average generation length: ~420 tokens (peak 1024)
- Desired SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end lat <= 250ms for streaming-enabled responses at target concurrency (see below)
- Target steady-state throughput: 120 requests/minute (concurrent clients ~8–12), burst to 300 rpm for 5–10m windows

Proposed validation checklist (short):
1) Baseline non-streaming inference on A100 (batch size 1) — measure token latency, CPU/GPU utilization, mem usage
2) Streaming run (chunked) — confirm first-byte latency and per-chunk token emission (measure 50/95/99 pcts)
3) Concurrency sweep — run 1, 4, 8, 12 concurrent connections to find knee point for chosen GPU
4) H100 comparison for same workload — capture throughput uplift and delta in 95th token latency
5) Cost delta matrix — compute per-1M tokens cost for each GPU family with observed throughput
6) Fallback validation — test automatic fallback to smaller model variant under saturation

Deliverables we will provide after runs:
- Latency/throughput matrix (spreadsheet)
- Recommended reserved throughput figure (req/s) and headroom buffer
- Suggested GPU SKU for Dedicated pool and a rollout cadence

Next concrete asks for VectorMed: please share a representative request trace (single JSON with prompt + expected generation params) and approx traffic schedule for a typical hour and peak day. If you prefer, drop that into the linked perf harness (see link).

Attachments: throughput_checklist_v1.xlsx (checklist + measured fields), gpu_tradeoff_estimate_v1.pdf (early cost sketch)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Samir Rao <samir@vectormed.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@vectormed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T18:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo checklist: throughput targets, streaming & GPU path (VectorMed)

Laura — thank you, this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our end: 

1) SLO precision: when you say 95th pct end-to-end token latency <= 250ms, is that with streaming enabled (i.e., first byte measured) or full-response completion? Our priority is predominantly smooth first-byte + steady per-chunk cadence for UI.
2) Concurrency: 8–12 is a good steady estimate. Peak windows during batch ingestion (EOD jobs) could push to 40 concurrent but those are non-interactive and can be routed to a lower-cost compute tier.
3) Cost target: keep platform inference spend below $0.60 / 1k tokens if possible (not strict, but a hard preference).

We'll upload a sample trace in the next 24 hours. Can you also run a quick sanity pass on L4-class for baseline cost comparison? If L4 can't meet first-byte SLO, we want to quantify tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

—Samir
Lead Product, VectorMed
samir@vectormed.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@vectormed.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@vectormed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo checklist: throughput targets, streaming & GPU path (VectorMed)

Samir — appreciate the clarifications. Short answers inline and updated asks below.

1) SLO measurement: we'll report both first-byte latency (when streaming is used) and full-response completion 95th pct. For the UI use-case you described, first-byte 95th pct is the primary signal; tentative target: first-byte 95th <= 180ms on H100, <= 240ms on A100 for the same concurrency. We'll validate these in the runs.
2) Concurrency profile: we'll include an ingestion-oriented run (40 concurrent non-streaming batch requests) and show routing recommendations (dedicated pool vs burst to shared capacity).
3) Cost target: we'll include per-1k-token cost numbers in the matrix and flag where we cannot meet the $0.60 / 1k tokens threshold. L4: yes — we'll add L4-class as a low-cost baseline test. Expectation: L4 may hit cost target but likely fail first-byte SLO for interactive flows; we'll quantify the deficit.

Immediate plan / timeline:
- Today: VectorMed uploads sample trace to the perf harness link.
- 48 hours after trace: Redwood runs 3 x verification runs (A100 baseline, H100 run, L4 baseline).
- Results: consolidated matrix + recommendation within 5 business days.

Follow-ups we need from internal ops (cc'd Marcus & Neha): please provision a 4-hour test window across the three SKUs in the staging Dedicated pool and reserve the perf harness compute. Note: we want to capture both streaming (low-latency) and batch ingestion (high-concurrency) patterns.

Thanks — Laura
